name: Resume after change approval (awaiting_approval → executing)
description:
The dev loop SHALL NOT start until a human approves the generated change (run.change.approved). This rule is the release side of the first human gate: a run parked in awaiting_approval returns to executing only once run.change.approved is present, at which point dev_from_task becomes eligible for the run's tasks. Without the approval fact the run stays parked — the gate holds. Rule-owned transition (G2). CONTRACT (design D15): group 5's approval adapter MUST stamp run.change.approved on the RUN entity (subject = agent.run.entity-id), or the run never resumes.

MUTUAL EXCLUSION with the CANCEL rule (nl-conversation-intent grp3-review M2): the run.change.rejected length_eq 0 guard is LOAD-BEARING, not decorative. The exact-command fast-paths bypass the NL routing rules' both-facts-absent guard and stamp a gate fact directly, so an authorized `/semdev reject` then `/semdev approve` on a still-gated run can leave BOTH gate facts present. This rule and run-lifecycle/07 each require the OTHER fact ABSENT, so a run holding both transitions to NEITHER instead of both resuming and cancelling. CALLED HONESTLY (grp5-review, semstreams M3): that outcome is an UNSURFACED STALL, not a park — nothing stamps run.awaiting.human, nothing posts, and the run simply sits at awaiting_approval with no human-visible signal. It is strictly safer than a double transition, and parking it is NOT the fix: a park at this gate is unrecoverable (both release rules require run.awaiting.human absent and nothing ever removes it — the B1 wedge). Recorded as a known gap in the design's Risks. Evaluated over ONE atomic mirror snapshot, which is why the partition lives in the rules (G2) and not in a Go guard racing them.

on_enter.reason: human approved the change; resuming to develop from the approved tasks
